name: POSEIDON
label: POSEIDON (GeneralDussDuss)
description: Keyboard-first pentesting firmware for the M5Stack Cardputer-Advance (ESP32-S3). 163 features across WiFi, BLE, sub-GHz, 2.4GHz, LoRa/Mesh, IR, LAN/network, BadUSB and recon, plus 'Argus' — an autonomous handshake-hunting gotchi. Same family as Bruce / Evil-M5Project / ESP32Marauder, built around a real QWERTY keyboard instead of a D-pad. Includes RF-transmit attacks (a 2.4GHz CW/broadband 'Data Flood Jammer' + a sub-GHz CC1101 jammer, deauth, BLE spam) — flash-and-study for an authorized lab only; jamming is illegal to transmit (FCC 47 U.S.C. §333).
note: GeneralDussDuss/poseidon. The Cardputer-Adv factory image (poseidon-factory.bin) is a merged single .bin flashed at 0x0 — the exact offset the project's own web installer uses (esp-web-tools manifest.json, chipFamily ESP32-S3, part offset 0). The sibling poseidon-launcher.bin asset is the M5Launcher app-slot variant (0x10000) and is intentionally NOT matched by asset_match, so a flash always writes the full standalone image. The ESP32-C5 'TRIDENT' satellite is a separate chip and a 3-file flash (bootloader@0x2000/partitions@0x8000/app@0x10000); it is not shipped in the latest release, so it is out of scope for this profile. danger=illegal-tx: unlike the Marauder/Bruce multi-tools, Poseidon ships a real 2.4GHz CW/broadband 'Data Flood Jammer' + a sub-GHz CC1101 jammer among its 163 features, so it follows the repo convention that every jammer-bearing firmware (bluejammer_esp32/bluejammer_bw16/nrf_bluenullifier2) is illegal-tx — matching safety.py _ILLEGAL_TX_KEYWORDS (broadband/jam) and 47 U.S.C. §333. Per the label-never-block doctrine the capability is retained + labeled, not removed; CC flashes firmware only (protocol=null → CC authors no TX and drives no jam command). Real-hardware flash owner-gated.
